Asking them to come to a cabin in the woods is quite another.

As a child some great influences of mine came from adults talking to me.

One was a musician. Be me, ten yo, alone on the train with my instrument. A man in the seat opposite to me says "it's a fun instrument to play, isn't it", he says he plays the same instrument, and takes his case from the rack. If you want I'll give you a concert just for you. I nod. I follow him to the part between compartments (were the doors are, not sure what it's called). Turns out he's a really great and well known folk musician. I've gone to plenty actual concerts of his since. That really encouraged me to exercise and play music.

The other one was a temp teacher and scientist, but not my teacher. I was about 15 back then. He was a really weird guy, always travelling, taking long trips on research boats. No fixed address, no fixed e-mail (changed when he changed jobs), no fixed telephone (changed country a lot). We had hour-long talks about science, he showed me experiments with equipment he'd hired or gotten from work. I wasn't the only one, some of my friends also came along. He ended up marrying an Italian when he was on holiday there, and last I heard that's still were he is.

 

When I was on holiday some years back I had some local children ~13 yo give me a tour of their town and join me on a hiking trip (without telling their parents, I discovered later). I'm a science nerd and I love nature a lot, so I really enjoyed talking to them about those things (and I hope I encouraged them a little). In the evening one of them invited me to have dinner with her and her family (that's when I discovered they weren't aware of anything, awkward). They were very inquisitive (understandably so!), but also very friendly. I was slightly weirded out when she wanted me to join her on the trampoline, and was very glad when she proposed to introduce me to her pets as an alternative. I'm still friends with two of them, we sometimes play videogames online and I visit them when I go on holiday in that region once every few years.

On another occasion I went on a trip to a research center for a week with a group of students. It was a mix of uni students and high school students. There was this one girl who seemed a bit shy and was often alone, so I talked to her. She was intelligent like nothing I'd ever seen in a girl her age (12, 13 maybe) so we talked about physics and chemistry a lot. I gave her some of the scientific magazines I bought (when I was done with them). The center was in the alps, so we hiked quite a bit. She wasn't very quick so I encouraged her to keep up the rhythm. In the evenings she would come to the dormitory I slept in to wish me goodnight (that was so cute).

 

I would be much more afraid of such things now. I've been influenced greatly by adults taking the time to encourage me. And I like to think I've done the same for a next generation. And I'm scared of a world were people can't interact with children for fear of being labeled a pedo. There's just things parents can't do when it comes to encouraging children. External role models can have a disproportionate influence.

 

EDIT: fixed a typo, clarified that we play video games over the internet

I'd also like to add that the young physics loving girl really made me realize that I want children some day. I don't like the concept of the first ~6 years, but teaching them to read with good literature, encouraging music, going for hikes, doing a stargazing session and nudging their inquisitive minds to ask questions about the universe, and conceive answers to those questions themselves is something I'm really looking forward to. I already had quite some experience as my sister is a decade younger and I went through all of those things with her.
